growth: The list of transferring-escalation conditions grows only at a retro, never by an agent's judgement in the moment (ADR-0071 ruling 5). Each condition is something a tool decides from recorded data, not something an agent judges; a fifth condition joins this file by being named at a retro and carrying its own predicate and remedy.
arbiter_source: Condition 1 names the arbiter a transferring escalation reaches. It is the *implementing* seat's — whichever seat did the work, never the implementer row for every seat (ADR-0071 ruling 4 as amended by A1, #361). Two callers resolve it two ways, and the difference is the composition point, not a disagreement: tools/brief.py supplies dispatch.escalation_head, the tabled head alone, because a briefing states who the table names before any loop exists; tools/review_loop.py's escalate path supplies arbiter.resolve_dispatchable, which walks the entry head, the entry tail and then the preference list, excluding on four rungs in order: a profile the registry does not carry, the routing refusals its caller passes, the profiles the issue's dispatch records place on the work, and the profiles the dispatch ladder would refuse now (selection, breaker, off-peak, credential). The registry rung was missing from this sentence until round 3 of #361. The caller resolves and supplies it either way, so this data never carries a profile name that drifts. A seat with no entry resolves to none and condition 1 stays silent: A1 struck the blanket fable-high fallback, so an arbiter nobody chose is not reached.

conditions.name: review_stuck_after_three_rounds
conditions.remedy: Three fix-and-re-review rounds have not cleared a finding above Low. Transfer the item to the arbiter named in the emission (resolved from the implementing seat's escalation entry, head first); the pre-declared landing default applies only after the arbiter adjudicates what remains, and every finding the arbiter does not dismiss is filed on the originating issue (ADR-0071 ruling 4).

conditions.name: two_consecutive_same_class_stuck
conditions.remedy: Two consecutive items of one routing class each reached the three-round state, which is evidence the items are under-specified rather than mis-implemented. Re-plan this item rather than re-fixing it (ADR-0071 ruling 5).

conditions.name: retry_on_new_profile_stuck
conditions.remedy: A second implementation attempt, from a clean base on a different profile, itself reached the three-round state, which distinguishes a bad item from a bad implementation. Re-plan the item rather than dispatching a third attempt (ADR-0071 ruling 5).

conditions.name: plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green
conditions.remedy: This item declares the #181 shape (routing class 4): a diagnosis whose plausible wrong fix would also go green, which no mechanical gate distinguishes. Transfer it to a fable seat for diagnosis; ruling 5 permits this escalation precisely because the gate cannot catch the wrong answer (CLAUDE.md's Seats and profiles section; #181).
